# Dong Dai

> Associate Professor in the Department of Computer and Information Sciences at the University of Delaware, leading the Data Intelligence Research Lab (DIRLab). Research on data-intensive and high-performance systems: parallel file systems, metadata management, graph storage, resource scheduling, and machine learning for systems.

Homepage: https://daidong.github.io/ — publications, teaching, students, and projects.

## Paper reports

Plain-language walkthroughs of the group's papers. Each page carries the verbatim abstract, the key findings, the BibTeX entry, and links to the paper itself.

- [LayerCheck: Adaptive Layer-wise Checkpointing for Large Language Model Post-training (Cluster '26)](https://daidong.github.io/papers/layercheck/): LayerCheck is a layer-wise adaptive checkpointing framework for large language model post-training: during training it tracks how much each transformer layer has actually changed and writes only the layers whose accumulated update crosses a threshold, and after a failure it rebuilds a full training state from the most recent saved copy of each layer — cutting total checkpoint size by up to 22.6× and end-to-end training time by up to 1.31× while the recovered run stays within 0.54% of the failure-free loss.
- [STELLAR: Storage Tuning Engine Leveraging LLM Autonomous Reasoning for HPC Parallel File Systems (SC '25)](https://daidong.github.io/papers/stellar/): STELLAR is an autonomous, LLM-driven tuner for HPC parallel file systems: it reads the parameters out of the file system manual, analyzes an application's Darshan I/O trace, proposes a configuration, reruns the application to measure it, and adjusts — reaching near-optimal Lustre settings within five attempts instead of the hundreds to thousands of runs classical autotuners need.

## Blog

Notes on systems research, agentic LLM systems, and academic life.

- [Agent Memory: Accuracy, Cost, and Gaps.](https://daidong.github.io/blog/long-context-didnt-kill-agent-memory/) (2026-06-23): With 1M-token context windows, agent memory no longer wins by beating full context on short histories. Its clear value today is cost; persistence and learning remain open problems.
- [Agent Reliability Is a Systems Problem: Checking Claims Against the Work Record](https://daidong.github.io/blog/provcheck-claude-agent-reliability/) (2026-06-18): A follow-up on agent-system reliability: why checking whether an agent's claims are supported by its own trace, files, and git state is different from checking whether the work is correct.
- [Black-box Characterization of LLM Serving Caches: Contracts, Asymmetries, and Prompt Design](https://daidong.github.io/blog/black-box-llm-serving-caches/) (2026-06-06): A black-box measurement of DeepSeek, OpenAI, and Anthropic prompt caches: why prefix identity matters, where provider contracts differ, and how prompt layout becomes a systems interface.
- [Will AI bankrupt my lab?](https://daidong.github.io/blog/will-ai-bankrupt-my-lab/) (2026-05-01): A shared API key, a negative balance, and a harder question for research labs: if frontier-model access becomes part of the cost of doing research, who pays for the tokens?
- [Auto Research Is Real. It's Just Not What People Think.](https://daidong.github.io/blog/auto-research-where-we-are/) (2026-04-11): Auto research is real and getting better fast. But it's not replacing researchers — it's changing where human effort matters. After months of building these systems, here's what I've learned about verification, deskilling, and taste.
- [Introducing Research Copilot — An AI Lab Partner for Academics](https://daidong.github.io/blog/introducing-research-copilot/) (2026-04-11): Research Copilot is an open-source AI desktop app built for PhD students, postdocs, and faculty — it searches literature across four databases, writes papers with verified citations, runs data analysis, and helps draft grant proposals, all in one place.
- [Introducing RAM Desktop — A Research Assistant That Works With You](https://daidong.github.io/blog/introducing-ram-desktop/) (2026-03-14): RAM Desktop is a macOS research assistant that breaks your question into tasks, collects evidence, and advances the work round by round — pausing at key checkpoints for your review.
- [University Isn't a Job Factory — and Computer Science Isn't Ending](https://daidong.github.io/blog/university-not-a-job-factory/) (2026-02-28): Two recurring fears: universities should be industry pipelines, and AI is ending software jobs. I think both framings are wrong — and the reasons why matter.
- [Hello World — Reviving My Personal Site](https://daidong.github.io/blog/hello-world/) (2026-02-19): After years of redirecting to Google Sites, I finally rebuilt my homepage from scratch. Here's why and what's next.
